intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Dallas County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: During our evaluation, another issue came to our attention that would warrant disclosure in this report. Other Issue: Five checks, totaling $189,401, were altered and cashed from the County's Operating Fund account on September 4, 2024.
verdicts.detail: A limited review (a “financial and compliance report”), not a full audit: the financial statements in it are unaudited. The letter continues in the report on page 3; parts that concern staff positions are left to the report, since this site doesn’t single out non-elected staff.

limits: From the 2024 report, dated September 30, 2025. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.

cities.name: Carthage
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer. Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer Former Recorder/Treasurer Christopher Ogburn, who resigned on June 1, 2023, was not removed from Town bank accounts at the time of his resignation. Subsequently, he made unauthorized cash withdrawals, totaling $52,500, from two Town bank accounts from April 11 to May 28, 2024. Ogburn entered a negotiated plea of guilty to Theft of Property on December 17, 2025; was sentenced to 120 months probation; and was ordered to pay restitution totaling $50,200.

cities.name: Fordyce
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of District Court Clerk. District Court Clerk The District Court Clerk was in noncompliance with Ark. Code Ann. § 16-10-209 in that bank reconciliations were not prepared, and disbursement journals were not properly maintained and reconciled to bank withdrawals.

cities.name: Sparkman
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer. Mayor The governing body did not review the prior report and accompanying comments and recommendations at the first regularly scheduled meeting following receipt of the report, as required by Ark. Code Ann. § 10-4-418.
